newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity slides on cash, cooler SW temps.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity slides on cash, cooler SW temps.

text.p: The NYMEX electricity complex slid Wednesday, sparked by softer cash market prices and outlook of cooler temperatures moving across the Southwest through the end of the week.
"It was overdone yesterday," said a California-based futures trader.
The May California-Oregon Border (COB) and Palo Verde (PV) contracts, which expire Friday, gave back some of yesterday's gains after the complex failed to extend Tuesday's rally.
May COB futures settled down 56 cents at $13.55 after hitting a high of $14.30. June COB finished down 73 cents at $12.35. Deferred COB months ended 25 to 79 cents lower.
May PV settled down 65 cents at $18.23 after posting a new life-of-contract high at $19.00. June PV finished down 91 cents at $18.35. Other PV contracts ended down 10-72 cents.

Cash power values in the West eased from Tuesday's levels on forecasts of cooler temperatures in the Southwest, but they were cushioned by firm swing natural gas prices and Bonneville Power Administration refraining from selling peak, next-day power, traders said.
Price spread of daily firm, peak power at COB tightened a dollar today to $18.50-19.50, and at PV narrowed two dollars to $22.00-23.00.

According to Weather Services Corp, temperatures in the Southwest would average 12 to 24 degrees below normal across the Rocky Mountains and near normal across Arizona, southern Nevada and California through Sunday.

Temperatures in the Pacific Northwest were forecast at three to six degrees below normal in the mountains and near normal elsewhere through Friday, rising to five to 10 degrees above normal regionwide by early next week.
Spot electricity prices could face downward pressure from power plants exiting unplanned and scheduled outages, market sources said.

Two coal-fired units, rated at 550 MW each,at the Jim Bridger power complex in Wyoming are scheduled to resume operation today. and 408 unit at the coal-fired Craig power plant in Colorado is said to restart tomorrow.
About 10,000 megawatts (MW) of coal and nuclear generating capacity in the West are currently offline.
Brokers and traders said May power futures could continue to be volatile as players keep tabs on the direction of cash trading and expiration of the May Henry Hub natgas futures.
